records.text: The Black Sea Rotational Force 2010 established a base at Mihail Kogălniceanu Airfield in Romania and began a three-month engagement there on May 17, 2010.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Well, for the first time that year, the Black Sea Rotational Force 10 goes out to Romania, and they establish the Mihail Kogălniceanu, I hope I'm saying that right, Kogălniceanu, probably not, air base in Romania. ... You can see that here. Marines, sailors, and sailors of the Black Sea Rotational Force 2010 officially kicked off their three-month engagement in the Black Sea region in a ceremony at Romania's Mihail Kogălniceanu Airfield on May 17th. Now, what's incredibly interesting, and we're going to get more into that.

verification.notes: Official Marine reporting confirms a three-month Black Sea Rotational Force engagement began May 17, 2010 at Mihail Kogalniceanu Airfield. It describes deployment to an existing Romanian installation, not establishment of a new base, so that phrase is overstated.

sources.title: Black Sea Rotational Force Officially Kicks Off
sources.relevance: Official Marine report confirms May 17, 2010 start, three-month engagement, and deployment to the existing airfield.

records.text: The United States announced a military base in Romania in 2010, and the Black Sea Rotational Force arrived that year.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: In 2010, when this is all going down, the United States announces, hey, we're going to put a military base out in Romania. ... Obviously, I'm oversimplifying here, but that's effectively what took place. And we know that in 2010, the Black Sea rotational force arrives and so does Tyler Bowyer.

verification.notes: Official Marine Corps records confirm that the Black Sea Rotational Force first deployed to Romania in 2010. They do not substantiate the statement's separate claim that the United States announced a new Romanian military base in 2010; U.S.-Romanian access arrangements predated that deployment.

sources.title: U.S. Marines, sailors arrive in Romania
sources.relevance: Official contemporaneous confirmation of the May 2010 BSRF arrival.

records.text: An article said six Marines from Reno in Black Sea Rotational Force 11 trained military forces in Eastern Europe in counterinsurgency techniques.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Let's now pick up in 2011, okay, so the Black Sea rotational force is doing their thing in Constanta. And I just want to stress how interesting it is to me that the majority of the men are coming from Reno, Nevada, the capital of casino and gambling laws are loosening up in Romania or actually rather monopolizing, I should say, in Romania. And here is an article which mentions that the chosen Marines were sent majority from that area. ... And has trained militaries in Bulgaria, Romania and Macedonia with both lectures and applied experience in ways to handle situations ranging from riot control to roadside bombs, blah, blah, blah, tells us at a glance a unit of six Marines, six Marines from Reno, part of the Black Sea Rotational Force 11, have been training military forces in Eastern Europe. OK, they're training them in counterinsurgency techniques.

verification.notes: Official Marine Corps records verify a Black Sea Rotational Force 2011 deployment, but the specific cited article about six Reno Marines and its exact counterinsurgency description could not be located. Search results only recirculated the episode's wording.

records.text: Erika Kirk said she went to Romania in 2013 because an extended-family cousin was part of the Black Sea Rotational Force and showed her orphanages and a hospital that troops had helped.
records.speaker: Erika Kirk

appearances.snippet: The reason why I even went over there is that one of my on my dad's side, his extended family like a cousin, he was a part of. ... a B-Surf over there. ... that's I went over there in 2013 and when he was over there we did we we did the same thing like he showed us these are the orphanages we work with these are the this is the hospital that we helped rebuild like amazing amazing humanitarian things that no one talks about that our troops are doing over there

verification.notes: A current transcript copy preserves Erika Frantzve's quoted account of a 2013 Romania trip prompted by a BSRF relative and visits to orphanage/hospital aid efforts. Public charity reporting independently supports her Romanian Angels partnership with U.S. Marines, though not the relative's identity.

records.text: The Black Sea Rotational Force 13 deployed from February through August 2013 as a special-purpose Marine air-ground task force.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And we know the Black Sea Rotational Force is going to be deployed for six months. Again, this will be BSRF 13. ... They kind of name it after the year it is. from February to August as a special purpose marine air ground task force.

verification.notes: Romania's Ministry of National Defence reported the August 8, 2013 closing ceremony after a six-month BSRF 13 exercise led by U.S. Marine Forces Europe. Contemporary and military descriptions identify the rotation as a special-purpose Marine air-ground task force running February to August 2013.

sources.title: Romanian Ministry of National Defence - BSRF 13 closing ceremony
sources.relevance: Official source confirms the six-month exercise and August 2013 close under U.S. Marine leadership.

records.text: Owens said the Black Sea Rotational Force established a Romanian base in 2010 that was later accused of trafficking and prostituting children.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: 2010 being the very year that the Black Sea Rotation of Force set up a base in Romania, which would subsequently be accused of trafficking and prostituting children.

verification.notes: Official U.S. military reporting confirms the Black Sea Rotational Force began operating at the existing Mihail Kogalniceanu Airfield in 2010. Romanian reporting confirms later allegations of an underage prostitution operation at the base, but the force did not establish a new base and the allegations were not proven.
